# Turn Meeting Notes into a Summary, Decisions and To-Do List with DeepSeek

> **In short:** Paste your rough meeting notes into DeepSeek with a reusable instruction, then ask follow-up questions to get a summary, the decisions made, and a to-do list with owners. Always check the result against your notes, because the AI only knows what you typed.

You will learn how to turn messy, half-finished notes into a clean follow-up that everyone can act on. This guide is for people who already use DeepSeek for simple chats and want a repeatable method for work meetings.

## Before you start

- **A DeepSeek account** and a way to open it, such as the website or the app. You already know how to start a chat and send a message, so those basics are assumed here.
- **Your rough notes** from a meeting, typed or copied into a plain text document. Rough is fine: fragments, arrows, and half-sentences all work.
- **Permission to share the notes.** Check your workplace's rules about which AI tools may see work information. If you are unsure, remove client names, pay figures and private details first.
- **About 15 minutes** for your first run. Later meetings take much less time.

## Step 1 — Tidy up your notes before you paste them

Open your plain text document and read through your notes once. Fix obvious typos, put each topic on its own line, and delete side chatter that has nothing to do with the meeting. If a name is sensitive, swap it for a role, such as "the finance lead," so you do not share more than you need to.

Keep the names of the people who will own tasks, because the to-do list depends on them. Your notes do not need to be neat. The AI works best when each point is clearly separated from the others, so a short line per idea is enough.

If the notes are on paper, type them up now. Handwriting that you cannot read will become guesses in the summary.

You'll know it worked when every topic from the meeting has its own line and you can read the whole document in about one minute.

## Step 2 — Write a reusable instruction, not a one-off question

This is the step that makes the process repeatable. Instead of asking a loose question, you write one instruction that you can reuse every time. Good instructions say three things: what role the AI should play, what the input is, and exactly what output you want, in what order.

Write your instruction in your notes app so you can copy it later. Keep it short and specific. Telling the AI to "say 'not stated' when information is missing" is one of the most useful lines, because it stops the AI from inventing owners or deadlines.

Your instruction does not need any special feature. It is simply text you paste at the top of the chat. Most people keep one version for team meetings and a shorter one for quick calls.

💬 Example: "You are helping me follow up after a team meeting. Below are my rough notes. Write a summary in five sentences or fewer, then list the decisions made, then list action items as owner, task, and due date. If an owner or due date is not in the notes, write 'not stated.' Do not guess. Here are my notes: [paste your notes here]"

You'll know it worked when your instruction is saved somewhere you can copy it in one click next time.

## Step 3 — Send your notes with the instruction

Open a new chat in DeepSeek. Paste your full instruction first, then paste your tidied notes below it, and send the message. The instruction goes at the top so the AI reads it before the notes.

Once you send it, the reply usually appears below your message, a few lines at a time. Wait for it to finish before you judge the result. Long meetings may produce a longer answer, and that is normal.

If the reply comes back as a single block with no sections, you probably forgot the list order in your instruction. Send a short follow-up such as "Please reorganize this into three labeled sections: summary, decisions, action items." If the reply looks cut off, ask it to continue from where it stopped.

You'll know it worked when you see three parts: a short summary, a list of decisions, and a list of action items with owners.

## Step 4 — Ask a follow-up question in the same chat

This is the multi-step part. In the same chat, the AI can see your earlier answer and build on it. Use that to make the to-do list more useful. For example, you can ask it to group tasks by person, so each owner can find their own work quickly.

Read the action items and look for two things: any task that has no owner, and any decision that sounds different from what you remember. Ask a direct question about them. The AI handles focused requests much better than general ones.

Keep the chat open, because your follow-up depends on it. If you start a brand-new chat, the AI will not remember the earlier summary, and you would have to paste everything again.

💬 Example: "Group the action items by owner. For anyone with no owner listed, add a line that says 'owner needed' so I can ask in the team channel. Keep the original wording of each task."

You'll know it worked when each person's tasks appear together and any unowned task is clearly flagged.

## Step 5 — Check the result against the original notes

AI summaries can miss a point or put a sentence into the wrong category. Before you share anything, compare the output with your notes, line by line for the decisions and action items. This is your job, and it takes about five minutes.

Ask the AI to show its work, which helps you check faster. Ask it to list each decision next to the note line it came from. If a decision has no matching line in your notes, delete it or confirm it with someone who attended.

Be extra careful with due dates and numbers. Dates are easy for the AI to misread, so verify every one.

💬 Example: "For each decision and action item you listed, tell me which line of my notes it came from. If a decision does not clearly match any line, mark it 'please verify.'"

You'll know it worked when every decision and task in the final list matches something you actually heard in the meeting.

## Step 6 — Turn the checked list into a message and save the template

Ask DeepSeek to write the follow-up email. Tell it who the email is for and how formal it should be. Copy the result into your email program, read it once more, and send it yourself. The AI cannot send messages or create tasks in your other apps, so the sending step is always yours.

Finally, save your instruction from Step 2 in your notes app with a label such as "Meeting follow-up template." Next time, copy it, paste your new notes, and repeat Steps 3 through 5. Over a few meetings, the process will take you about ten minutes.

💬 Example: "Write a short follow-up email to the team summarizing the decisions and action items below. Use a friendly, professional tone and end with a request to reply if anything is wrong. Send it as from [your name]."

You'll know it worked when you have a sent follow-up email and a saved template you can reuse.

## Common mistakes

- **Trusting the first answer without checking.** The AI can misread a name or invent a deadline. The fix is to always compare the output with your notes, especially owners and dates.
- **Starting a new chat for every follow-up.** The AI forgets earlier answers in a new chat, so you end up repeating yourself. The fix is to keep working in the same conversation until your list is final.
- **Pasting sensitive information without checking the rules.** Work notes can contain client names, pay figures or private details. The fix is to check your workplace policy first and remove anything that does not need to be there.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use the same method after a family planning call or a school committee meeting. You get a clear list of who agreed to do what, without hunting through a messy page.
- **For your business or work:** Keep one saved instruction for all your team meetings. Each follow-up takes minutes, and no task slips through because it was buried in a long set of notes.
- **If you want to go further:** Try building a short template for each meeting type, such as a weekly status call or a client review, with different output sections for each. Once the templates work, test whether a shorter instruction gives you the same quality.

**What the tool cannot do:** DeepSeek cannot attend your meeting, hear what was said, or confirm that your notes are accurate. It works only with the text you give it, and it can still make mistakes, so a human must review the final list.

## Try it now

Take the last set of notes you have, even if they are messy, and paste them into DeepSeek with this line at the top: "Summarize these notes in five sentences, then list decisions, then list action items with owner and due date, and write 'not stated' for anything missing." Read the answer and check one decision against your notes.
